newsitem.title: UK: UK priest sacked after supermarket stealing row.
newsitem.headline: UK priest sacked after supermarket stealing row.

text.p: A London priest who provoked a storm by declaring that stealing from supermarkets was justified said on Saturday he had been sacked.
John Papworth, an unpaid assistant Church of England minister, hit the headlines in March by describing shoplifting as "a badly needed reallocation of economic resources".
Papworth, 75, also admitted helping British double agent George Blake to hide from police after his escape from jail in 1966.

Papworth said he had received a letter from the archdeacon of Charing Cross saying that his permission to officiate as a Church of England minister was not being renewed because his comments on stealing from supermarkets had caused "considerable misunderstanding".
Papworth told Reuters he was shocked at the decision.
"Really it has devastated me. They haven't taken on board the seriousness of the issues I was raising about the great economic power of big supermarkets."

Papworth denied he was encouraging people to steal but said he was pleased at raising the issue over the "moral status" of huge shopping developments which were taking over from small community based shops.
